# A complete cash purchase: the bank and the expense, no payable.
#
# `Assets:Bank:USD −100.00` against `Expenses:Supplies:USD +100.00`. The bill
# side of the cash sale — an entry with the expense breakdown baked in, which
# has nothing on a payable to link to a bill.
#
# Expenses are the other side of what this entry already records, so naming
# that split would move the purchase onto the payable: the cost gone from the
# P&L, the bill reading paid, the entry still balancing.
#
# The expense account is opened here because the bill book's `Expenses:Supplies`
# is CAD, and a CAD split would make the entry convert — which is a second
# reason to refuse and would leave it unclear which one fired. Everything here
# is USD, so only the account's type says no.
#
# What this fixture produces: a USD transaction, bank −100.00 against
# `Expenses:Supplies:USD` +100.00, neither split in a lot.
#
# Verified by
# tests/integration/test_linking_a_split_not_on_the_receivable.py.
2026-01-01 open Expenses:Supplies:USD
	type: Expense
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
2026-03-26 * "Cash purchase, expense baked in"
	guid: "7f8a9b0c5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e"
	currency.mnemonic: "USD"
	Assets:Bank:USD -100.00 USD
		guid: "8a9b0c5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
	Expenses:Supplies:USD 100.00 USD
		guid: "9b0c5f6a7b8c9d0e1f2a3b4c5d6e7f8a"
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
